description: Personal dosimeter. Logs cumulative radiation dose for the UI.
Potassium iodide. Grants temporary radiation resistance while active.
Decorporation medication. Cleanses a chunk of current radiation dose.
Filters airborne fallout from the lungs. Moderate protection, degrades with use.
Full-body protective suit. High radiation protection, degrades with use.
Replacement cartridge for purifying contaminated water.
Replacement filter for the shelter air-filtration unit.
Quenches thirst, but contaminated. Drinking it adds a dose of radiation.
Preserved rations. Restores hunger and a little morale.
Combustible fuel for the heater and generator.
Salvaged fabric. Used to craft bandages and filters.
Salvaged metal parts. Used to craft filters and gear.
Sterile dressing. Restores health when used.
Uncooked meat from mutated fauna. Slightly contaminated; cook before eating.
Cooked meat. Hearty meal that restores hunger and a little morale.
Contaminated water. Boil or filter it before drinking.
Assembled medical supplies. Restores a large amount of health when used.
Cell pack for geiger counters and dosimeters. Without power, instruments go dark.
Reference sources and tools to recalibrate a geiger or dosimeter. A mis-calibrated counter lies.
Fine forceps for extracting shrapnel and dressing deep wounds. Needed for full gunshot care.
Broad-spectrum pills. Treat bacterial infections and dysentery before they become sepsis.
Gold and stones from before. Pretty until the sky burns; then it buys nothing.
Pre-exchange notes. Still foldable. Not drinkable.
Boards, wire, and cracked vacuum tubes. Needed to repair instruments and the purifier.
A cracked photovoltaic panel pried off a weather station. It still charges, slowly, on the four hours a day the ash thins enough to let light through.
Solvents and reagents scavenged from labs and garages.
Portable receiver. Often dead. Still full of boards worth stripping.
A scavenged vehicle engine. Repair it, feed it fuel and parts, and drive out of the ash.
Threaded suppressor. Extremely rare loose loot. Usually already mounted on mil/rebel/specialist weapons.
IR-capable laser aiming module. Usually already mounted on mil/rebel/specialist weapons.
Angled/vertical grip for recoil control. Usually already mounted on mil/rebel/specialist weapons.
High-magnification optic. Usually already mounted on mil/rebel/specialist weapons.
Holographic CQB optic. Usually already mounted on mil/rebel/specialist weapons.
Flip dual-magnification scope. Usually already mounted on mil/rebel/specialist weapons.
Empty hull. Scrap or reload feedstock.

Tripod-mounted .50 cal HMG. Provides massive hatch defense bonus when stock is on hand and the gun is mounted + oiled. Requires 2 operators to fire at full efficiency; jams without oil. Two crew + a stock pile of this weapon is the difference between a held hatch and a breached one.
Corroded cal_9x19 rounds. Scrap only — not safe to fire.

Sawn timber block. Framing and fuel.
Bound pages. Morale, kindling, or knowledge.
Burned wood. Filters and slow heat.
Hard coal. Long burn for heaters.
White crystals. Cooking and bad morale swaps.
Dry cement. Needs 1L water for hatch/shelter work.
Two metres of rope. 0.4M per use.
Glass tube. Old radios and quirks.
Drains 0.2KG/use. Alone: 1 quality dinner. +carrot+potato+2 water: 4 quality dinners.
Quest item. Do not open lightly.
Hard stone. Below guns in barter.
A sealed envelope, yellowed and brittle. The stamp is from a country that no longer exists. Someone wrote this to someone they loved, and it never arrived.
A childs drawing on the back of a ration card. Stick figures of a family. A sun with rays like bent spokes. A house with smoke coming out of the chimney. The paper is singed at the edges.
Tinted lenses in a rubber frame. The strap is frayed but holds. Cuts the glare off the ash-fields and makes the horizon stop hurting.
Compact double-action sidearm. Lightweight and easily concealed.
Rotary-locking .380 ACP sidearm. Low recoil compact pistol.
Surplus military pistol. Robust Tokarev variant in 7.62×25mm.
Extended capacity Tokarev pattern sidearm. Chambers 7.62×25mm.
Classic submachine gun. High rate of fire in heavy .45 ACP.
Polymer-framed tactical SMG. Hard-hitting .45 ACP suppression.
Super V recoil-mitigation submachine gun. Blistering fire rate in .45 ACP.
Ultra-compact pistol-class variant of the APC45 in .45 ACP.
Swiss tactical submachine gun. Precision engineered in .45 ACP.
Submachine gun with high-capacity quad-stack magazine in 9×21mm.
Ultra-compact machine pistol with extreme rate of fire in 9×21mm.
Modern polymer submachine gun. Highly adaptable SMG in 9×21mm.
Pre-war milled submachine gun. Fine craftsmanship in 7.65×21mm.
Machined steel submachine gun. Durable vintage SMG in 7.65×21mm.
Auto-regulating gas-operated 12-gauge shotgun. High tactical reliability.
Classic semi-automatic 12-gauge hunting shotgun. Soft recoil and steady cycling.
Long-recoil operated 16-gauge shotgun. Humpback receiver legend.
Lightweight aluminum-alloy 16-gauge shotgun. Easy field handling.
Military carbine with STANAG mag compatibility. Standard issue 5.56 rifle.
Short-stroke gas piston assault rifle. High reliability in harsh ash.
Modular 5.56 assault rifle with folding stock and full-length top rail.
Bullpup 5.56 assault rifle. Compact overall length with full barrel reach.
Iconic 7.62×39mm assault rifle. Machined receiver, extreme field tolerance.
AR-style platform feeding from AK magazines. Heavy 7.62×39mm punch.
Squad automatic weapon with heavy barrel and bipod in 5.45×39mm.
Short-barrel carbine variant in 5.45×39mm. Compact close-quarters rifle.
Right Arm of the Free World. Full-power 7.62×51mm battle rifle.
Roller-delayed blowback 7.62×51mm battle rifle. Heavy hard-target punch.
Integrated suppressor-ready PDW carbine in .300 Blackout.
Ultra-short barrel tactical carbine chambered in .300 Blackout.
Compact Daniel Defense AR-platform PDW chambered in .300 Blackout.
Bullpup PDW with 50-round translucent top magazine in 5.7×28mm.
Compact PDW with folding foregrip and armor-penetrating 4.6×30mm.
AR-platform personal defense weapon chambered in 4.6×30mm.
Modernized tactical PDW platform chambered in 4.6×30mm.
Long-stroke piston marksman rifle chambered in 7.62×54R.
Precision bolt-action sniper rifle chambered in .338 Lapua Magnum.
Long-range competition sniper rifle chambered in .338 Lapua Magnum.
Bullpup precision sniper rifle chambered in .338 Lapua Magnum.
Extreme long-range anti-materiel sniper rifle in .408 CheyTac.
Take-down modular sniper chassis chambered in .408 CheyTac.
Heavy anti-materiel precision platform chambered in .408 CheyTac.
Semi-automatic anti-materiel rifle chambered in 12.7×99mm NATO (.50 BMG).
Heavy magnetic ballast. Required to run indoor grow-lights without blowing the shelter's fuses.
Highly pressurized. Keeps the Arcology cryo-pods from rotting. Handle with extreme caution.
Slit-carved wood and leather. Prevents Snow Blindness. The world narrows to two thin lines.
Silicone compound. Essential for repairing frozen pipe joints and electronics. Stays pliable at -60C.
Highly radioactive, frozen ash-water. Cobalt isotopes detectable on a Geiger counter. Proof of the Salting.
Heavy, lead-lined. Stamped with Central Command serial numbers. The physical evidence of Protocol Zero.
Allows scavengers to carry 3x weight in deep snow. Requires immense stamina to pull. Leaves deep tracks.
Lanolin and alcohol. Stops the necrosis, but the pain is blinding. Apply to affected extremities.
High-pressure brass valve. Required to tap into deep-crust heat. One mistake and the room floods with steam.
Lithium hydroxide. Scrubs carbon dioxide from sealed bunker air. Your lungs will thank you.
Heavy, treated wood. Essential for preventing cave-ins during subterranean expansion. Smells of creosote and desperation.
Compressed ash and fungal binders. Smells awful, but provides excellent radiation shielding. The Rot Farmers' signature product.
Soda-lime cartridge. Filters out CO2 and hydrogen sulfide in deep tunnels. Breathe easy — for forty minutes.
A sample of the toxic aquifer. Proof of the deep-earth fracturing. The liquid is thick, iridescent, and smells of almonds and sulfur.
A 50m spool of copper wire connected to a surface dosimeter. Allows mapping rad-pockets without entering them. The clicks tell you where death lives.
Grows on the Sunken Grid. Provides dim, cold light without batteries. Calms those afraid of the dark. The Dredgers cultivate it like livestock.
Heavy mining tool. Required to safely excavate collapsed rubble without triggering secondary cave-ins. The compressed air hisses like something alive.
Reverse Osmosis filter. The only thing that can strip the Black Aquifer's chemical toxicity. Each use degrades it by 20%.
Pressurised canister of copper sulfate. Clears a room of Ash-Blight spores instantly. The mist is acrid and stains everything blue-green.
A watertight blade from the Sunken Grid. Contains pre-war tectonic survey data. The Dredgers trade these for UV lamps to treat their rickets.
A fiberglass rod with a steel tip. Essential for probing UXO fields without setting off pressure fuzes. One wrong angle and you lose a foot.
Woven copper and silk. Shields electronics from EMP and magnetic anomalies. The only thing between your dosimeter and a lie.
A wind-up metronome rigged to a speaker. Draws automated sentry fire until the barrel melts. The ticking is the loneliest sound in the wastes.
Pre-war military processing board. Highly susceptible to EMP rot. The Custodian's brain, extracted from a dead sentry.
Acoustic foam panels. Lines the shelter walls to reduce AcousticSignature. Silence is survival when the machines are listening.
A localised electromagnetic pulse. Fries sentries and drones, but ruins your own dosimeters. A necessary betrayal of your own instruments.
AP round penetrator. Required to craft armour-piercing ammo to pierce Custodian chassis. Dense enough to stop a tank. Or a drone.
High-pressure air line. Used to repair automated turrets or shelter airlocks. The hiss of compressed air is the sound of something still working.
A heavy, encrypted brass key. Disables the Dead Hand protocol in a local sector. The war ends here, one switch at a time.
Active noise-cancelling. Protects against acoustic warfare and tinnitus. The world goes quiet when you put them on — and that's the point.
High-pressure resin gun. The only way to stop Concrete Cancer without tearing down the wall.
Zinc-coated steel. Resists carbonation. Essential for deep structural repairs.
Heavy, dark glass and lead mesh. Prevents Affliction_CornealBurn during Ozone Scourge.
Darkened silica. Crude but effective UV protection for surface camera feeds and periscopes.
A toxic nightshade. The raw ingredient for the Lethe Protocol amnestics.
Mood stabilizer. Keeps the Waking Sickness at bay, but causes severe thirst and tremors.
Silvered glass. Used by the Sun-Seekers to reflect the Scourge, or to signal distant factions.
A pristine magnetic disk. Contains the backed-up social media of a dead city.
Heavy canvas and steel cable. Used to secure Bunker-Born to the hatch during surface exposure.
Rendered from Ash-Whale roots. Replaces degraded pre-war plastics for water seals.
Crude Lethe substitute. Consuming prevents MentalBreak but adds Affliction_LiverToxicity.
Pre-war audio recording. Sacred relic to Bunker-Born.
Photos of sunshine, grass, and smiling strangers.
Heavy vinyl records from the Before.
Surface camouflage and UV scattering suit.
A pre-war hatch seal, still supple. One more winter it might hold.
Fast-setting repair compound. Smells like wet dust and ammonia.
Electrical tape, mostly intact roll. Keeps the shorts in the walls where they belong.
A working pre-war engine. Heavy enough to argue with. Worth more than the car it came from.
Sealed bearings in grease paper. Drills and pumps die without them.
One metre of pre-war copper pipe. The well does not care how scarce it is.
